title: A three year backtest on NQ is mostly a test of whether the NASDAQ went up
author: person-person12
selftext:
I ran a popular 10am opening range strategy on NQ 1m from july 2023 to feb 2026, 100k account, one contract. 535 trades, 60.2% win rate, net -$3,675.

Then I split those same trades by what the market was doing underneath them. **The only conditions it made money in were uptrends**: 152 trades, 1.08 profit factor, +$3,307. The 280 trades that landed in volatile conditions lost $6,764, and taking the uptrend trades out of the set leaves nothing behind them.

The window is doing most of the work there. Mid 2023 to early 2026 on the NASDAQ is close to a straight line up, so anything long biased is going to look like it has something in that range. Buy and hold took 100k to roughly 170k over the same period while this did -3.7%, so the strategy spent three years fighting the only thing that was reliably paying.

Its like testing an umbrella by carrying it around Vancouver for a month and deciding its a great umbrella. You havent learned much about the umbrella, youve learned that it rained.

What I do now is run the rules over the longest history the instrument has and read the result broken out by regime instead of as one net number. In [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) that breakdown comes out with the run, so a 1.08 in one kind of market sat next to a 0.93 in another is visible before you decide anything.

The split exists in the trade log either way. It just doesnt show up if the only line you read is the one at the top.
